strengths: Opening balcony scene is concrete and immediately answers why the street looks like a postcard.
Visitor tips are usable: ask the host, watch drips, do not photograph neighbors’ laundry.
Exceptions (rain, pollen, condos, coin laundry) prevent a one-note myth.

issues.location: Intro + What Visitors Are Actually Seeing + Cost/Space + FAQ + closing
issues.problem: The same thesis—dryers exist; this is not folklore—is restated so often that a reader who already got it in paragraph three may skim or drop mid-article.
issues.suggestion: Keep the anti-myth once in the short answer, once in FAQ, and once in the close. Let the middle be household logistics (washer location, drips, futon, rules).

issues.location: Cost, Space, Sun, and the Futon Problem — “engawa-adjacent space”
issues.problem: engawa is dropped without a gloss; first-time visitors may bounce.
issues.suggestion: One parenthetical: a traditional veranda, or simply “a covered porch.”
